hero.headline: Flesh-eating cattle parasite spreads beyond Texas as new screwworm cases found
hero.body:
A flesh-eating parasite that infests livestock has spread beyond its initial Texas detection site, with authorities now confirming cases in both Texas and New Mexico. The New World screwworm fly, which had been eradicated from the United States decades ago, has reemerged after more than 50 years and now threatens the nation's cattle industry.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed three additional screwworm infections on Monday, including two more cases in Texas and one in New Mexico. The Texas cases involved a calf in La Salle county and a goat in Gillespie county. The initial cases were discovered in Zavala county, located southwest of San Antonio, where two infections were found approximately five miles apart.

The screwworm fly lays eggs in open wounds on animals, and the hatching larvae then feed on living tissue, causing a painful condition called screwworm myiasis. If left untreated, the infection can kill the host animal. The parasite affects cattle, livestock, and wildlife, though federal officials have confirmed that the U.S. food supply remains safe, as screwworms do not infest meat, fruits, vegetables or other food sources.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott issued a statewide disaster declaration on Friday, warning that it is likely to be "an extraordinarily challenging summer" for infected areas. Abbott said state officials were working with the federal government to slow the spread of the fly.

Authorities have launched an aggressive containment response. Officials are dispersing millions of sterile screwworm flies in the vicinity of the initial infections. These sterile male flies prevent wild female flies from reproducing, a method that has proven effective for controlling and eradicating the pest when combined with enhanced surveillance, movement restrictions, and prompt treatment of wounds.

The Texas Animal Health Commission noted that it had been actively preparing for a potential resurgence of the parasite for over two years. The director urged all animal owners and caretakers to remain vigilant for the presence of larvae in animal wounds and to immediately report any suspicions.

Animal movement restrictions are now in effect to prevent further spread of the pest. The USDA discovered the second infestation after testing a number of suspect cases, according to the agency's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.

The parasite's arrival poses a significant economic threat to U.S. cattle ranchers. A widespread resurgence could lead to animal deaths as well as higher labor and treatment costs. The situation has already impacted border trade. The U.S. had closed its southern border to live cattle imports from Mexico for over a year as the disease moved northward, contributing to a contraction in the beef industry to a 75-year low. Additionally, Canada announced a temporary ban on livestock from Texas following the confirmed infections.

cards.headline: Israel and Iran halt attacks after Trump intervention
cards.body:
Israel and Iran have agreed to pause military strikes following an appeal from President Trump to "immediately stop shooting." Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the halt in a televised speech, stating that "at present, the fire on this front has been halted" after Iran was struck and stopped attacking. However, Netanyahu vowed to respond "with force" if Iran attacks again.

The temporary ceasefire comes after a significant escalation in which Iran launched approximately 30 ballistic missiles at Israel, prompting Israeli retaliatory air strikes on Iranian targets including defense systems and a petrochemical complex. This marked the most direct confrontation between the two nations since an April ceasefire.

Both countries have emphasized their readiness to resume hostilities if necessary. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tehran would not tolerate what it called "repeated violations," warning that "Iran's response will remain the same" without genuine efforts to build trust. Israel's defense minister stated that Israel would continue operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon and strike Beirut if the militant group attacked Israel.

Analysts describe the new ceasefire as extremely fragile, with multiple potential flashpoints for renewed escalation. The agreement does not address underlying disputes between the nations, and significant complications remain unresolved.

A key tension point involves Lebanon, where Israel has been conducting operations against Hezbollah, an Iranian ally. Israel has rejected Iranian attempts to link any permanent ceasefire to halting its Lebanon offensive. Netanyahu faces domestic pressure and an election later this year to continue degrading Hezbollah's capabilities. Reports indicate Hezbollah continued firing rockets into northern Israel even as the ceasefire was announced.

The escalation has had broader consequences. Oil prices surged five percent during the violence, raising concerns about global fuel costs and economic impacts. Stock markets rose when both sides announced the halt.

Trump has pressured Israel to stop attacks in Lebanon to create space for diplomatic negotiations. In recent communications with Netanyahu, Trump has been explicit about his demands for de-escalation. The president posted on social media that both countries wanted an "immediate CEASEFIRE" and that "final negotiations on 'Peace' are proceeding."

Iran has signaled skepticism about American intentions, with a foreign ministry spokesperson saying Tehran was exchanging messages with Washington in an atmosphere of "extreme suspicion." Iran also accused Israel of sabotaging diplomacy through its Lebanon operations.

The Houthis, Yemen-based militia allies of Iran, have pledged to continue targeting Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea, suggesting the broader regional conflict remains volatile. Their control of strategic shipping routes adds economic dimensions to the security concerns.

The situation continues to require active diplomatic management to prevent renewed hostilities between Israel and Iran.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping visits North Korea to reassert Chinese influence
cards.teaser: Chinese leader Xi Jinping traveled to North Korea in a rare visit aimed at reminding Kim Jong-un that China remains the senior partner in their alliance.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in North Korea for a two-day visit, his first in nearly seven years. The trip aims to strengthen ties between the two countries, which have grown strained as North Korea has moved closer to Russia.

Xi's visit signals China's effort to reassert its influence over its longtime ally. The meeting between Xi and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un underscores China's attempt to maintain its traditional role as North Korea's primary backer amid shifting regional dynamics.

cards.headline: Airline profits expected to halve as fuel costs jump $100 billion
cards.body:
Global airline profits are projected to drop by half this year as jet fuel costs have surged due to Middle East conflicts disrupting oil supplies. The International Air Transport Association reports that fuel expenses have climbed significantly over the past year, placing severe financial pressure on carriers worldwide.

Airlines are already taking concrete action to manage the crisis. Two million airline seats have been cut from May schedules as carriers redraw their operations in response to soaring jet fuel prices. About 13,000 fewer flights will operate globally next month, according to aviation analytics company Cirium, representing less than 2 percent of global aviation capacity. Istanbul and Munich have recorded the biggest drops in flights, with Turkish Airlines and Lufthansa making substantial cuts. Lufthansa has eliminated 20,000 short-haul flights operated by its CityLine subsidiary.

Budget airlines face particularly acute challenges from the fuel price spike. These carriers operate on thin profit margins and have less flexibility to absorb cost increases compared to larger legacy airlines. However, some budget operators have committed to maintaining full summer schedules. EasyJet and Wizz Air have pledged to operate their summer schedules despite pressure on the unhedged portion of their fuel bills. Most major short-haul airlines operating from the UK are well hedged on jet fuel, meaning they do not expect immediate cost increases.

The industry has limited options to hedge against sharp price movements, and the increases arrive at a time when many carriers were still recovering from previous economic disruptions. Fuel typically represents one of the largest operating expenses for airlines, often accounting for a quarter or more of total costs.

The UK government has introduced contingency measures to manage potential summer disruptions. The transport secretary agreed with the aviation industry on unusual measures including consolidating schedules on routes with multiple daily flights to the same destination. Airlines can now cancel flights with fewer seats sold without losing valuable operating rights for the following season. UK refineries have been asked to maximise jet fuel production under contingency planning, though ministers have resisted industry requests to cut taxes or reduce environmental rules.

International agencies have predicted that Europe faces jet fuel shortages if Middle East disruptions continue. Analysts at Goldman Sachs warned that the UK is particularly vulnerable as Europe's largest net importer of jet fuel, with low inventory levels and reduced domestic refining capacity. UK stocks could fall to critically low levels, potentially requiring rationing measures.

The projected profit decline will be felt across the airline industry, though impacts will vary based on individual carriers' fuel hedging strategies, route structures, and ability to pass costs to consumers through higher ticket prices. The combination of rising fuel costs and operational constraints raises questions about whether some carriers, particularly smaller operators, will sustain operations if fuel prices remain elevated.

cards.headline: Europe faces prolonged economic slowdown as Iran war continues
cards.teaser: European economic recovery prospects dim as the conflict with Iran points to extended period of elevated prices and reduced growth.
cards.body:
Europe is watching its economic recovery fade as the ongoing war with Iran shows no signs of quick resolution. Analysts now project a prolonged period of higher prices and slower growth across the continent rather than the sharp but brief shock initially anticipated.

The persistent conflict has disrupted energy markets and supply chains, creating lasting headwinds for European economies. Economic indicators point to sustained challenges ahead as businesses and consumers adjust to the new environment of elevated costs and reduced certainty about future conditions.

cards.headline: Jeffries conditions FISA renewal on removal of acting intelligence chief
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he will not vote to renew the nation's warrantless surveillance powers unless President Trump removes Bill Pulte as acting Director of National Intelligence. Jeffries made the statement as Congress faces a deadline to reauthorize Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which allows intelligence agencies to monitor communications of foreign targets without a warrant.

"Reversing the Bill Pulte appointment is a starting point, not an ending point," Jeffries said of the battle to renew Section 702. The Democratic leader's position adds a significant political obstacle to the reauthorization process, as the minority party's cooperation is typically needed for major intelligence legislation to pass.

The Section 702 program has been a source of ongoing debate between privacy advocates and national security officials. Intelligence agencies argue the tool is critical for monitoring foreign threats, while critics have raised concerns about its potential use to collect information on Americans without proper oversight. The program requires periodic reauthorization by Congress.

Pulte's appointment as acting DNI has drawn scrutiny from Democrats who question his qualifications for overseeing the nation's intelligence apparatus. The acting director position gives Pulte authority over multiple intelligence agencies and access to the nation's most sensitive classified information. Democratic concerns about his leadership appear to have crystallized around the FISA renewal debate.

The standoff sets up a potential clash between the White House and congressional Democrats over both personnel and surveillance policy. Without Democratic support, passage of FISA reauthorization could face significant hurdles in the House, where the minority party has leverage on national security matters that typically require bipartisan backing. The outcome will test whether Trump is willing to make changes to his intelligence leadership team to secure the surveillance authorities his administration seeks.

cards.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B visa fee
cards.teaser: A judge has struck down the Trump administration's requirement that companies pay $100,000 for each H-1B visa application, ruling the fee unlawful.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Boston has invalidated Trump's $100,000 annual fee for H-1B visa applications, ruling the policy violated federal administrative law and the Constitution. The decision came in a lawsuit filed by 20 Democratic state attorneys general challenging the fee announced in September, which represented a 20-to-50 fold increase over existing rates.

Judge Leo Sorokin's 42-page ruling vacated the sweeping fee requirement. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister claims election victory in test of Russian influence
cards.teaser: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan declared victory in an election viewed as a referendum on the country's orientation toward the West and away from Russia.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan claimed victory in Armenian elections that were widely seen as a test of Russia's influence in the former Soviet republic. The vote comes as Armenia has pursued closer ties with Western nations and distanced itself from Moscow.

The election results suggest Armenian voters have endorsed Pashinyan's pro-Western direction despite pressure from Russia. Armenia has traditionally been within Russia's sphere of influence, but recent years have seen the government seeking new partnerships with Europe and the United States. The outcome could accelerate Armenia's pivot away from Moscow and reshape regional alliances in the South Caucasus.

cards.headline: Pope and Spanish Prime Minister meet, both in opposition to Trump
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met after both recently clashed with President Trump, though their motivations appear to differ.
cards.body:
Pope Francis addressed the Spanish parliament, calling for moral renewal in public institutions to uphold human dignity. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez hosted the pontiff during the visit, which included the historic papal address to the legislature.

The Pope emphasized the importance of respect for inherent dignity in all people, speaking directly to lawmakers about ethical leadership in government and public life.

cards.headline: Judge orders return of Colombian woman mistakenly deported to Congo
cards.teaser: A U.S. judge reversed an earlier decision after determining a Colombian woman was improperly deported to Congo by the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A U.S. judge has ordered the return of a Colombian woman who was incorrectly deported to the Democratic Republic of Congo by the Trump administration. The judge ruled that the deportation was improper after reviewing the case.

The decision represents a reversal of the judge's previous ruling on the matter. The woman's mistaken deportation to the wrong continent highlights issues with deportation procedures under the current administration. The judge has now mandated that she be brought back to the United States.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance criticized over comments on UK stabbing
cards.teaser: British officials accused Vice President JD Vance of stoking division after he blamed migration for a murder whose perpetrator was recently sentenced to life in prison.
cards.body:
British officials criticized Vice President JD Vance for comments about the murder of Henry Nowak, saying Vance was attempting to create division in the United Kingdom. Vance attributed the killing to what he called a migrant invasion. The killer was sentenced to life in prison last week.

British authorities said Vance's remarks were inappropriate and divisive. The comments represent another instance of tension between the Trump administration and a traditional U.S. ally. The case has become a flashpoint in debates over immigration policy in both countries.

cards.headline: Mexican artisans speak out on World Cup jersey production claims
cards.teaser: Indigenous women in Mexico addressed claims that Adidas exploited them to produce World Cup jerseys after viral videos sparked outrage.
cards.body:
Indigenous artisans in Mexico have responded to viral videos alleging that Adidas exploited them in producing World Cup jerseys. The claims sparked outrage among Mexicans concerned about mistreatment of the women involved in the work.

Journalists visited mountain communities to hear directly from the artisans about their experience creating the jerseys and their working conditions. Their firsthand accounts shed light on the production process and have reignited debate about how to balance celebrating Indigenous craftsmanship with ensuring fair treatment in commercial manufacturing.

cards.headline: Six people injured in stabbing at Penn Station, suspect in custody
cards.teaser: Authorities arrested a suspect after six people were injured in a stabbing incident at Penn Station in New York City.
cards.body:
Six people sustained injuries during a stabbing attack at Penn Station in New York City. Law enforcement took a suspect into custody following the incident at the busy transportation hub.

At least one victim has spoken publicly about the attack. Penn Station serves as a major transit center connecting commuter rail lines and subway services in Manhattan. The incident occurred near Madison Square Garden, raising questions about security protocols at the facility.

cards.headline: Magnitude 6.1 earthquake strikes off Cuba, shaking felt in Florida
cards.teaser: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake occurred near Cuba, with residents across southwest Florida reporting feeling tremors from the event.
cards.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake occurred near Cuba, with residents across southwest Florida and other parts of the state reporting felt shaking from the temblor. The quake's seismic waves traveled hundreds of miles from the offshore epicenter.

The National Weather Service confirmed the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to the United States. Earthquakes of this magnitude typically cause structural damage near the epicenter but weaken significantly with distance.

cards.headline: Pentagon revises military religious affiliation categories after Mormon lawmakers object
cards.teaser: The Defense Department updated its list of recognized religious affiliations following backlash from lawmakers over changes to how it categorizes Christian denominations.
cards.body:
The Pentagon updated its list of recognized religious affiliations following backlash from Mormon lawmakers and Utah Republicans. The revision addressed changes to how the military categorizes Christian religious groups, including The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

The Trump administration released the updated religious categories list four months ago before quickly withdrawing it without explanation. The Pentagon's decision to revise the classification system followed objections from members of Congress representing areas with significant LDS populations.

cards.headline: Updated California primary results show county-by-county votes in governor's race
cards.teaser: Updated vote tallies reveal how each California county voted in the gubernatorial primary, with Democrat Xavier Becerra advancing to November.
cards.body:
Updated vote counts show the distribution of support across California counties in the state's gubernatorial primary election. Democrat Xavier Becerra will advance to the November general election after the primary results.

California's vote counting process extends for days after Election Day as counties process mail-in ballots and verify signatures. The state's election system allows ballots postmarked by Election Day to arrive and be counted in subsequent days, contributing to the extended timeline for final tallies. Nearly a week after the primary, updated results provide a clearer picture of regional voting patterns across the state's 58 counties.

cards.headline: England cricket officials investigate nightclub incident involving captain Ben Stokes
cards.teaser: The England and Wales Cricket Board is investigating a nightclub incident involving England cricket captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson.
cards.body:
England's cricket board is investigating a breach of team protocols following an incident involving captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson at a London nightclub in the early hours of Monday. The incident occurred shortly after England secured a convincing victory over New Zealand in the first Test at Lord's.

The England and Wales Cricket Board and Saracens rugby club are both looking into the matter. The players could potentially miss the second Test against New Zealand as a result of the investigation.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO oversubscribed ahead of Wednesday close
cards.teaser: Wall Street banks report strong demand for SpaceX shares as orders are set to close on Wednesday.
cards.body:
SpaceX is launching what's being called the biggest stock market debut in history, with shares set to release on June 12 at a $135 valuation. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising $75 billion from the offering.

Demand for the IPO has significantly outpaced supply, with orders exceeding available shares ahead of Wednesday's closing deadline. Wall Street banks are giving their wealthiest clients priority access to the listing, underscoring how major IPOs serve as key tools for wealth management divisions to attract and retain high-net-worth clients.

cards.headline: Sam Bankman-Fried formally seeks presidential pardon
cards.teaser: The imprisoned FTX founder has officially applied for a pardon from President Trump.
cards.body:
Sam Bankman-Fried, the former FTX cryptocurrency exchange leader serving a 25-year sentence for fraud, has formally applied for a presidential pardon from the Trump administration. The pardon request was officially submitted on Monday.

Bankman-Fried was convicted of defrauding customers and investors in connection with FTX's collapse, one of the most significant financial frauds in recent years.

cards.headline: Stock markets rebound as chipmakers recover from selloff
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted gains as technology stocks bounced back from recent losses.
cards.body:
U.S. stock indexes rose on Monday as semiconductor and technology shares bounced back from recent sharp declines. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both advanced, with investors regaining interest in artificial intelligence stocks after the previous week's losses.

Chipmaker shares led the market recovery after experiencing significant selloffs. Geopolitical developments also supported the rally, as Iran and Israel signaled a pause in military hostilities following weekend strikes. The combination of reduced tension in the Middle East and renewed appetite for tech equities drove the positive trading session.

cards.headline: Oil prices ease after initial spike on Iran-Israel attacks
cards.teaser: Oil markets pulled back from earlier gains after both Iran and Israel indicated they had halted military operations.
cards.body:
Oil prices retreated from their highs Monday after Iran and Israel announced they were halting military operations. Iran had launched approximately 30 missiles at Israel in response to a strike in Lebanon, prompting Israel to conduct two waves of air strikes in Iran. The initial attacks had driven crude prices sharply higher due to concerns about potential supply disruptions in the oil-rich Middle East region.

As both nations signaled a pause in hostilities, energy markets eased from their peak levels. The volatile trading reflected investor uncertainty about whether the ceasefire would hold, given the region's critical importance to global oil production.

cards.teaser: European economic recovery prospects dim as the conflict with Iran points to extended period of elevated prices and reduced growth.

cards.headline: Energy-importing nations shift focus to domestic production
cards.teaser: Countries are prioritizing domestic energy development to insulate themselves from volatile global markets.
cards.body:
The Iran war is pushing energy-importing countries to turn inward and prioritize domestic energy sources. Governments are seeking to protect their economies from the volatility in global oil and natural gas markets caused by the ongoing conflict.

The strategic shift represents a longer-term response to supply uncertainty and price swings that have disrupted economic planning. Nations previously reliant on imports are accelerating investment in domestic energy infrastructure and production capacity to reduce exposure to geopolitical risks in major producing regions.

hero.headline: Apple unveils redesigned Siri AI and iOS 27 at WWDC 2026
hero.body:
Apple introduced a revamped voice assistant and operating system updates at its annual Worldwide Developers Conference on Monday morning at Apple Park. The event, which marks CEO Tim Cook's final WWDC with the company, featured announcements spanning Siri AI, iOS 27, and expanded Apple Intelligence features.

The company debuted Siri AI, a more conversational version of its voice assistant that incorporates a two-tiered AI model powered by Google technology. The new assistant includes features designed to make interactions feel more natural and contextual. Apple also announced AI-powered additions to several core apps, including Safari, Shortcuts, and its password management tools.

The updated Shortcuts app now allows users to describe desired workflows in text prompts rather than manually building automation sequences. Apple's Image Playground, the company's AI image generator, received a visual overhaul intended to improve its competitiveness with other generative AI tools. The Photos app will gain new AI editing capabilities, including a spatial feature called Reframe that lets users adjust image perspectives using artificial intelligence.

Apple announced that watchOS 27 will drop support for several older devices, including the Apple Watch Series 9, Ultra 1, and SE 2. The decision renders multiple generations of Apple Watches unable to run the latest operating system. The new watchOS includes Siri upgrades and health features focused on perimenopause tracking.

The weeklong event will continue with developer sessions and product demonstrations. The AI features announced are scheduled to roll out to users this fall alongside the new operating system releases. The conference comes as Apple works to integrate artificial intelligence capabilities across its product line while maintaining its focus on user privacy and on-device processing.

cards.headline: Google adds Gemini 3.5 to NotebookLM for premium users
cards.teaser: Google's NotebookLM tool is receiving an upgrade limited to AI Ultra and enterprise accounts.
cards.body:
Google has upgraded NotebookLM with Gemini 3.5 and introduced a new feature called Antigravity. These enhancements expand the capabilities of the AI-powered note-taking and research platform.

The upgrades are currently limited to AI Ultra and enterprise subscribers. There is no timeline for broader availability to other user tiers.

cards.headline: Pentagon identifies Chinese tech firms supporting military
cards.teaser: The Defense Department named Alibaba, Baidu, BYD, and Unitree as companies aiding China's armed forces.
cards.body:
The Pentagon released an updated list of Chinese companies it says support China's military operations. The roster includes e-commerce giant Alibaba, search engine Baidu, electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, and robotics firm Unitree.

The Trump administration previously released a version of this list four months ago but withdrew it without explanation. The Pentagon has now reissued the updated designations.

cards.headline: Researchers develop carbon capture material from polystyrene cups
cards.teaser: Scientists have found a way to convert used polystyrene into carbon-absorbing sponge material.
cards.body:
Researchers developed a process to upcycle polystyrene waste into carbon sponge material capable of capturing carbon dioxide. The technique transforms disposable cups and other polystyrene products into functional carbon capture tools.

The carbon sponge material could provide a dual benefit by reducing plastic waste while creating materials useful for environmental remediation. The research offers a potential application for the large volumes of polystyrene that typically end up in landfills.

cards.headline: Microsoft packages infected with credential-stealing malware for second time
cards.teaser: Security researchers found 73 Microsoft packages containing malware that runs when opened by AI agents.
cards.body:
Malicious code has been found in 73 Microsoft packages for the second time in recent weeks. The credential-stealing malware activates automatically when AI agents access the infected packages.

The self-replicating malware targets user credentials and spreads without requiring additional user interaction beyond opening the compromised package. The repeated incidents suggest a persistent vulnerability in Microsoft's package distribution system.

cards.headline: Artemis II astronauts receive patch commemorating Mach 39 flight speed
cards.teaser: The crew earned a new mission emblem recognizing their record-breaking velocity during the moon mission.
cards.body:
NASA's Artemis II crew members flew at Mach 39 during their mission and received a new patch marking the achievement. The emblem recognizes the extreme speeds reached during the lunar flight.

Measuring Mach numbers from space presents technical challenges, according to mission officials. The crew's velocity represents one of the fastest speeds achieved by humans during spaceflight operations.

cards.headline: Apple adds AI workflow builder to Shortcuts app
cards.teaser: Users will be able to create automation sequences by describing them in text prompts.
cards.body:
Apple announced new AI-powered features coming to its Shortcuts app this fall. The update enables users to build automated workflows by describing what they want the automation to do, rather than manually constructing each step.

This addition is part of Apple's broader rollout of AI capabilities across multiple apps, including Safari and the Password app. The enhancement makes workflow automation more accessible to users without technical expertise in building shortcuts.

hero.headline: Netherlands defender Jurrien Timber ruled out of World Cup with groin injury
hero.body:
Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber has been ruled out of the Netherlands' World Cup campaign after sustaining a groin injury. The Dutch national team confirmed the withdrawal, dealing a significant blow to their defensive lineup ahead of the tournament. Brazil forward Neymar is reportedly making good progress in his recovery from injury.

Timber, who plays for Arsenal in the English Premier League, had been expected to feature prominently in the Netherlands' World Cup squad. The 25-year-old defender's absence forces the coaching staff to restructure their defensive plans for the tournament. The groin injury proved severe enough to prevent his participation in the competition.

The timing of the injury compounds the Netherlands' preparations as the World Cup approaches. Timber's versatility as a defender who can play both center back and right back made him a valuable asset for the national team. His club experience in the Premier League had positioned him as a key player for the Dutch squad.

Meanwhile, Brazil received more positive news regarding Neymar's fitness. The forward has been working his way back from injury and is reportedly progressing well in his rehabilitation. His recovery timeline remains important for Brazil's World Cup ambitions, though specific details about his return were not provided.

The Netherlands will need to adjust their defensive strategy without Timber as they prepare for their World Cup fixtures. The injury creates an opportunity for other defenders in the squad to step into more prominent roles during the tournament.

cards.headline: England cricket captain Ben Stokes under investigation for nightclub incident
cards.teaser: The England and Wales Cricket Board is investigating an incident at a nightclub involving captain Ben Stokes, bowler Gus Atkinson, and a Saracens academy player.
cards.body:
England cricket captain Ben Stokes and pace bowler Gus Atkinson are being investigated by the England and Wales Cricket Board over an incident at a London nightclub in the early hours of Monday. The incident occurred shortly after England's victory in the first Test against New Zealand at Lord's.

The ECB is examining an alleged breach of team protocols. A Saracens rugby academy player was also involved in the incident, prompting Premiership Rugby to launch its own investigation. Both players could potentially miss the second Test against New Zealand.

cards.headline: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby granted injunction to play despite gambling admissions
cards.teaser: A court granted quarterback Brendan Sorsby a temporary injunction allowing him to play in 2026 despite admitting to gambling violations.
cards.body:
Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby received a temporary injunction permitting him to play in 2026 despite admitting to gambling violations. The court ruling allows Sorsby to participate while legal proceedings continue. Several Big 12 teams are reportedly considering not playing Texas Tech in response to the ruling.

Analysts have characterized the decision as compromising NCAA enforcement authority. The ruling creates questions about the future of NCAA enforcement mechanisms and their ability to impose penalties on athletes who violate gambling rules. The case has generated widespread debate about the organization's regulatory power.

cards.headline: Knicks season ticket holders face high-value Finals seats as prices reach thousands
cards.teaser: New York Knicks season ticket holders are confronting difficult decisions as NBA Finals seats carry values reaching thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
New York Knicks season ticket holders face tough decisions as NBA Finals seats at Madison Square Garden carry steep prices. The team announced a winning auction bid of one million dollars for two celebrity row seats, with a law firm securing a courtside seat through raffle contribution. Josh Hart criticized the ticket prices as unreasonable for fans.

The Knicks' winning streak has energized the city ahead of Game 3 at home. Ticket prices have fluctuated, with some declining after Donald Trump confirmed his attendance at the Finals games.

cards.headline: Manchester City continue talks with Chelsea to appoint Enzo Maresca as manager
cards.teaser: Manchester City are in ongoing negotiations with Chelsea to hire Enzo Maresca as their new manager.
cards.body: Manchester City are continuing negotiations with Chelsea regarding the appointment of Enzo Maresca as their new manager. The two Premier League clubs remain in talks as City works to secure their managerial target.

cards.headline: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen recovering at home after collapse
cards.teaser: Christian Eriksen said he is doing well and recovering at home with his family following his collapse during a match against Ukraine.
cards.body:
Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen is recovering at home with his family after collapsing during Sunday's match against Ukraine. Following the medical emergency on the field, Eriksen received immediate attention from medical staff.

The midfielder says he is "doing well" and has been able to leave medical care to return home, where he continues his recovery surrounded by family.

cards.headline: Former England player Theo Walcott expects Marcus Rashford to start at World Cup
cards.teaser: Former England winger Theo Walcott said Marcus Rashford is a certain starter for England at the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body: Former England winger Theo Walcott has backed Marcus Rashford to start for the Three Lions at the World Cup, describing him as a "dead cert" for the tournament. Walcott expressed his enthusiasm about Rashford's prospects with the national team.

hero.headline: Romy and Michele Sequel Enters Production for Hulu
hero.teaser: Mira Sorvino and Lisa Kudrow have begun filming a sequel to their 1997 cult comedy about two women attending their high school reunion.
hero.body:
The sequel to Romy and Michele's High School Reunion officially started production and will stream on Hulu. Oscar winner Mira Sorvino and Emmy winner Lisa Kudrow are reprising their roles from the 1997 cult classic comedy.

The original film followed two unsuccessful 28-year-olds who invented fake careers to impress former classmates at their high school reunion. The new production marks a long-awaited reunion for the two leads, nearly three decades after the original film became a comedy favorite.

cards.headline: Death of a Salesman Revival Wins Six Tony Awards, Leads 2026 Ceremony
cards.teaser: A radical new production of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman took home six prizes at the 79th Tony Awards ceremony on Sunday, leading an evening where no sin.
cards.body:
Director Joe Mantello's stripped-back revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman dominated the 79th Tony Awards, claiming six awards including best revival of a play. Star Nathan Lane accepted on behalf of the cast, describing the play as one that "continues to teach us who we are as humans and Americans."

Lesley Manville and John Lithgow won lead acting trophies at the ceremony. The musical wins were distributed among several productions, with Ragtime and Schmigadoon! also earning recognition. Mantello praised Miller's classic as a story that "still talks to us through time."

cards.headline: The Bear Final Season Trailer Released Ahead of June 25 Premiere
cards.teaser: The acclaimed restaurant drama will conclude with eight episodes releasing simultaneously on Hulu and FX later this month.
cards.body:
The Bear's final season will premiere on June 25, with all eight episodes dropping simultaneously on Hulu and FX. A trailer for the season has been released, depicting the restaurant staff preparing for one last dinner service.

The series, which centers on a Chicago restaurant and its team navigating the demands of fine dining, concludes with this upcoming season.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Says Audiences Would Not Accept Black Actor as James Bond
cards.teaser: The actor, who has long been the subject of casting speculation, stated that playing Bond is not realistic and some audiences will not accept a Black male in the role.
cards.body:
Idris Elba has dismissed speculation about him taking on the James Bond role, telling British GQ that the conversation linking him to the part was "never legit." The 53-year-old actor, currently promoting Masters of the Universe, stated that audiences would not accept a Black actor in the iconic spy role, suggesting cultural resistance to the casting.

Elba also pushed back against the idea of making James Bond more contemporary, saying he is against making the character "woke." His comments came after years of fan discussions about him as a potential successor to Daniel Craig.

cards.headline: For All Mankind Production Team Revives Apple Newton for Alternate History Series
cards.teaser: The Apple TV series works with the tech company to upgrade and feature the discontinued Newton device as its alternate timeline's version of the iPhone.
cards.body:
Every season of Apple TV's "For All Mankind" begins with the same creative meeting. Prop master Jaime Mengual sits down with co-creators Ben Nedivi and Matt Wolpert and producer Ben McGinnis to discuss a key element of the show: the Apple Newton.

The production team has made the discontinued device central to the series' alternate history timeline, positioning it as the equivalent of the iPhone in their reimagined world. This collaboration between the show and Apple represents a distinctive blend of product placement and historical storytelling.

cards.headline: NBA Finals Game 3 Tips Off at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks host the San Antonio Spurs as the series shifts to New York, with the Knicks seeking their first championship since 1973.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks returned home to Madison Square Garden for Game 3 of the 2026 NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs. This marks the first NBA Finals game New York has hosted since 1999.

Enhanced security measures were implemented for the game due to presidential attendance. The Knicks urged fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and to bring minimal belongings. The NYPD cancelled an outside watch party that had been planned for the venue, following discussions with the Secret Service. The decision came after arrests were made during celebrations outside MSG following Game 2.

cards.headline: Karolina Wydra in Emmy Consideration for Pluribus Role
cards.teaser: The actress nearly skipped her audition for Vince Gilligan's series but is now in awards contention after being cast as an alien character following a global search.
cards.body:
Karolina Wydra almost did not audition for Vince Gilligan's Pluribus but now finds herself in the Emmy race for her performance. The casting team had searched globally for an actor to play Zosia, a key character who must be beautiful, smart, calm and patient.

In the series, the alien hive mind sends Zosia to work with resistor and rebel Carol, played by Rhea Seehorn. Wydra, who had previously been typecast as a femme fatale, secured the role after the casting team was unable to find the right performer elsewhere. Her performance has generated awards consideration.

hero.headline: Jeffries conditions FISA renewal on removal of acting intelligence chief
hero.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he will not vote to renew the nation's warrantless surveillance powers unless President Trump removes Bill Pulte as acting Director of National Intelligence. Jeffries made the statement as Congress faces a deadline to reauthorize Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which allows intelligence agencies to monitor communications of foreign targets without a warrant.

"Reversing the Bill Pulte appointment is a starting point, not an ending point," Jeffries said of the battle to renew Section 702. The Democratic leader's position adds a significant political obstacle to the reauthorization process, as the minority party's cooperation is typically needed for major intelligence legislation to pass.

The Section 702 program has been a source of ongoing debate between privacy advocates and national security officials. Intelligence agencies argue the tool is critical for monitoring foreign threats, while critics have raised concerns about its potential use to collect information on Americans without proper oversight. The program requires periodic reauthorization by Congress.

Pulte's appointment as acting DNI has drawn scrutiny from Democrats who question his qualifications for overseeing the nation's intelligence apparatus. The acting director position gives Pulte authority over multiple intelligence agencies and access to the nation's most sensitive classified information. Democratic concerns about his leadership appear to have crystallized around the FISA renewal debate.

The standoff sets up a potential clash between the White House and congressional Democrats over both personnel and surveillance policy. Without Democratic support, passage of FISA reauthorization could face significant hurdles in the House, where the minority party has leverage on national security matters that typically require bipartisan backing. The outcome will test whether Trump is willing to make changes to his intelligence leadership team to secure the surveillance authorities his administration seeks.

cards.headline: Trump pressures Thune to fire Senate parliamentarian over voting bill
cards.teaser: President Trump called on the Senate majority leader to immediately fire the parliamentarian to advance legislation requiring citizenship proof and photo ID for voting.
cards.body:
President Trump called on Senate Majority Leader John Thune to immediately fire Senate Parliamentarian Elizabeth MacDonough. The move would remove a procedural obstacle to passing the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to cast a ballot.

The Senate parliamentarian serves as the chamber's rules expert and adviser on procedural matters. Firing the parliamentarian would be an extraordinary action, underscoring the administration's determination to reshape federal voting requirements.

cards.headline: Johnson questions California primary vote counting process
cards.teaser: Speaker Mike Johnson said the California primary election process raised concerns, citing continued vote counting weeks after polls closed.
cards.body:
Speaker Mike Johnson criticized California's primary election process, saying it "stinks to high heaven." His remarks echo complaints from President Trump and other Republicans about the state's election system, particularly its extended vote-counting timeline that continues weeks after Election Day.

Johnson's comments come as California continues tallying ballots in the gubernatorial primary. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are competing against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. The ongoing vote-counting process has also affected other races, including Los Angeles's mayoral contest, where results have shifted as ballot processing continues.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor receives limited tour of federal detention facility
cards.teaser: Governor Mikie Sherrill said she was granted access to a Newark immigration facility after weeks of requests but described the visit as closely controlled.
cards.body:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill said she received a "closely controlled and limited tour" of a federal immigration detention facility in Newark. The Democratic governor had been seeking access to the Delaney Hall facility for weeks before being allowed entry.

"After being denied access for weeks, I was finally allowed into Delaney Hall — but what I received was a closely controlled and limited tour of the facility," Sherrill said. The tour comes amid ongoing questions about conditions and operations at federal immigration detention centers across the country.

cards.headline: Jeffries outlines Democratic agenda on affordability if party wins majority
cards.teaser: The House Democratic leader said the party's first bill if it gains the majority would focus on lowering costs for Americans.
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said the first bill of a Democratic majority would tackle affordability issues. House Democrats have met privately for months to develop the specifics of legislation aimed at lowering costs.

The announcement signals Democratic priorities as the party positions itself for potential gains in future elections. Jeffries' focus on affordability reflects polling showing economic concerns remain a top issue for voters across party lines.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center excludes Trump from award ceremony invitations
cards.teaser: The performing arts venue dropped President Trump's name from invitations to its Mark Twain Award ceremony honoring Bill Maher.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center has removed President Trump's name from its website following a US district judge's order issued last month. The performing arts venue had previously featured references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" on its site.

The removal was completed Monday, ahead of a June 12 deadline set by the center's general counsel to eliminate all references to the president. The decision came in compliance with the court's ruling regarding the venue's official materials and website presence.

cards.headline: New York City increases security for Trump's NBA Finals appearance
cards.teaser: The city is tightening security measures ahead of the president's attendance at Game 3 between the Knicks and Spurs.
cards.body:
New York City has implemented enhanced security measures for President Trump's attendance at Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden. The Knicks are asking fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and to bring minimal belongings. The New York Police Department cancelled a watch party outside the venue following discussions with the Secret Service, a decision made after more than 20 arrests occurred at a similar gathering during Game 2.

The heightened security comes as the Knicks make their first Finals appearance since 1999, generating significant excitement throughout New York City. Presidential attendance at major sporting events requires extensive coordination between local law enforcement, the Secret Service, and venue security teams to ensure public safety.
